session: Hold bass and melody fixed through two chord changes. Retain one common tone while moving an inner voice toward a chosen destination; compare with stacked chord copies.
check: Hear the inner line, check section range/player density and remove a doubling that hides its arrival.

topic: Woodwind foreground handoff and breath gap
session: Let one woodwind carry a short phrase and another answer. Compare an overlapping handoff with a clear gap using verified short and sustained sources.
check: Check sounding octaves, attack delay, hidden breath and wet tails; label a generic fallback instead of claiming a recorded legato transition.

topic: Woodwind flourish with an arrival deadline
session: Write a brief upper run leading into a sustained chord tone before the next vocal or string entrance. Compare fewer pitches with a denser run.
check: Verify the final attack speaks before the deadline and the flourish yields the foreground; do not select speed solely from MIDI grid density.

topic: Library lookahead versus musical attack compensation
session: Compare the same articulation in available live and lookahead modes, retaining a reference hit and the next phrase. Inspect declared plugin latency before shifting MIDI.
check: Measure audible onset and confirm no doubled compensation, missing pre-roll note or changed release; report unsupported modes rather than invent controls.

topic: Acoustic drum articulation and intensity staircase
session: Map actual snare, rim, side-stick and hat variants. Play a soft-to-hard staircase, repeated equal hits and open-hat followed by closed-hat.
check: Check intended samples, velocity boundaries, alternates and choke; gain-scaled identical hits are not new recorded articulations.

topic: Metal kick reinforcement versus riff copying
session: Keep one guitar riff and cymbal pulse. Compare kick on its selected accents with kick on every guitar onset; retain the same snare pattern.
check: Listen with bass for rhythmic definition and low-tail collisions, then choose reinforcement by phrase role rather than event count.

topic: Metal tom fill landing and limb feasibility
session: Build a two-bar riff with a short snare-to-tom fill. Compare a busy final beat with a shorter fill that leaves time for the next cymbal.
check: Inspect simultaneous hand/foot roles and audition the first full bar after the fill; retain explicit electronic exceptions.

topic: DnB two-step and half-time backbeat comparison
session: At fixed project tempo make a two-step control with snare on 2/4, then a deliberately half-time backbeat variant. Keep kit and bass pitches fixed.
check: State the counted pulse and heard backbeat; check that tempo alone is not being used to label half-time.

topic: Break shuffle unit versus individual ghost slices
session: Identify a hat-plus-ghost gesture and its main snare. Resequence one version with the gesture intact and another with individual slices.
check: Compare internal pocket and neighboring tails at target tempo and after one transpose; keep an end marker and first downbeat.

session: Make a four-bar break with one kick displacement and one short final fill. Compare a fixed sustained sub with note lengths adapted around those hits.
check: Hear snare identity, bass pitch and the first return attack; reduce the competing tail before thinning the entire break.

topic: Garage backbeat omission and high-layer replacement
session: Use one kit and compare a normal two-step phrase with a removed backbeat replaced by quieter hat/percussion motion. Retain the same overall loop length.
check: Identify which missing accent changes the pocket; high-layer sample count and global looseness are not the goal.

topic: Brazilian club percussion displacement with a stable anchor
session: Use one verified scene reference and copy its anchor and displaced percussion positions. Compare the measured offsets against a uniform swing treatment.
check: Check exact beat basis and relative attack placement; do not generalize one shift rule to every Brazilian funk subscene.

session: From an annotated twelve-pulse reference, retain its cycle and remove accompaniment under one sung phrase, then re-enter at the measured location.
check: Verify cycle position and phrase close against the reference; a count without exact accent/onset evidence is insufficient to claim flamenco practice.

topic: Three-plus-five chord rhythm with a fixed topline
session: Compare four equally spaced chords with three-plus-five-beat durations over two bars; retain the same bass roots and top melody.
check: Reconcile held melody and bass at the shifted boundary; judge rhythmic shape before changing extensions or sound.

topic: Upper chord cluster with an open bass
session: Spell one minor-eleventh voicing. Compare its evenly spaced version with an upper semitone cluster while preserving a wider low register and the same pitch classes.
check: Inspect actual seventh quality and bass identity; choose cluster density by the melody and patch rather than sophisticated appearance.

topic: J-pop section seam into a temporary target
session: Join two short progressions. Compare the plain seam with an applied dominant or local ii-V into the new section, retaining its melody.
check: Verify defining altered notes and individual resolutions across the join; distinguish a momentary target from established modulation.

topic: Atmospheric intro and motif reveal budget
session: Make an eight-bar textural intro from verse harmony, then a second version that previews only a fragment of the chorus motif. Keep the later chorus unchanged.
check: Listen from intro through first vocal entrance and main motif reveal; name what is deliberately withheld rather than add every layer.

topic: Five-beat bar grouping without tempo automation
session: At one fixed quarter-note tempo compare 5/4 accents grouped 3+2 with ten eighths grouped 3+3+2+2. Retain the same total bar duration.
check: Identify accent grouping without reporting actual tempo fluctuation; inspect melody crossing the bar independently of accompaniment.

topic: Cumulative render pitch and independent bass reconciliation
session: Print a melodic layer, shift it by an octave and then by a known cent amount, while leaving bass unprinted. Record the cumulative result before retuning bass.
check: Verify actual stable pitches instead of filenames; compare source, transformed print and combined harmony without double-transposing printed content.

topic: 808 source root and two-source choke ownership
session: Map two tonal bass samples with verified roots. Compare independent groups with one intentional mutual choke group through a section change.
check: Check overlapping tails and a real note-off; do not rely on different group numbers or a zero-velocity trigger as proof of a cut.

topic: One-pitch composition through timbre and rhythm
session: Keep one written pitch class and build a short form using articulation, dynamics, register and instrument handoff. Compare a static-patch control.
check: Name the audible development without inventing chord changes; distinguish fixed pitch class from unchanged physical frequency.

topic: Fixed rhythm with probabilistic pitch correction
session: Retain one event rhythm while generating bounded pitch variants and a specified correction map. Capture one accepted run as editable notes and audio.
check: Compare event times across runs and verify saved/reopened and later-bar playback against the accepted capture.

topic: Stochastic fill capture with a guaranteed return
session: Keep three bars empty of fills, select one of several one-bar variants for the fourth and capture the accepted sequence into the timeline.
check: Check first beat after each fill, reproducible reopen/rewind and separation of live scene ownership from arranged playback.

topic: Feedback loop processing versus output-only color
session: Use one available delay's declared internal feedback path and a separate output EQ. Compare a supported feedback filter with output filtering at bounded level; if that filter is absent, state the dependency instead of adding a bus cycle.
check: Inspect whether regeneration changes or only delivered tone changes; a final limiter does not establish internal stability.

topic: Compressed wet piano as an intentional texture
session: Keep one piano phrase and compare reverb before heavy compression with reverb after it at matched delivered loudness. Add one controlled slow pitch movement.
check: Hear mechanical detail, wet-tail recovery and pitch center; preserve a dry source and avoid treating threshold extremes as neutral enhancement.

topic: Open-string pedal and moving shoegaze figure
session: Program reachable octave or fifth shapes over explicit open-string pitches, then compare restrained whole-chord bends with fixed tuning.
check: Check one sounding note per string, bend reset, dissonance and actual distortion density; a thirdless chord is not clash-proof.

topic: Found percussion into a playable melodic source
session: Choose an authorized recorded object, trim attacks/tails, verify stable root candidates and create a small playable mapping with explicit intensity layers.
check: Audition adjacent pitches and velocity boundaries; preserve inharmonic character when intended and do not call duplicate gain levels new takes.

topic: Generated stem addition with independent harmonic validation
session: Keep a separated source arrangement and add one generated or externally supplied instrumental phrase. Preserve the source and new file as distinct artifacts.
check: Verify alignment, pitch center, embedded room, seams and context before accepting; note extraction/generation provenance and listen to the complete edited section.

topic: Native string note gap touch and overlap control
session: At 120 BPM use the same available string source, D5 quarter note at @0 and E5 quarter note at @1.06, @1 and @0.94 in three separate bars. Keep velocity and written articulation fixed, then use the preferred join in a fourth bar with a cello and viola answer.
check: Compare the 30 ms written gap, touching gates and 30 ms overlap alone and in the ensemble. Confirm actual attack/release behavior; generic gate overlap does not establish a recorded legato transition.

session: One authorized dry sung phrase with clear consonants, one held vowel and a breath. A simple chord/drum bed and retained unchanged reference. Mark consonant onset, stable-vowel arrival and word exit by actual listening. Compare whole-word move with sparse vowel-centered timing edit while keeping preceding/following anchors. Compare independent pitch with preserved formants on only the stable intended note; retain expressive entry. Hear at final tempo, first exposed then with backing.
check: Vowel reaches intended beat without deleting its onset. No new lisp, doubled breath, wrong word or audible seam. Local pitch edit does not flatten unpitched consonants. No automatic phoneme labels, lyric editor or drift/vibrato curve tool is claimed. Monophonic pitch display/peak is evidence only; exact word ownership requires listening.

session: Supplied independent lead/unison takes, a chord-aware harmony and a held hum or open-vowel source. Two sections with different density. Assign unison width, vowel-bed sustain and answer/counterline roles before processing. Choose one leading breath and align intended shared consonants without zeroing every timing difference. Compare a genuine take with a labeled delayed-copy alternative, including mono fold. Remove each role from the completed mix with compensation and automate section subtraction.
check: Each kept layer loses a named musical function when removed. Harmony line fits actual chord changes rather than a constant semitone formula. Lead words remain clear; choir bed is not mistaken for independent singers made from duplicates. Use supplied/externally rendered takes; autonomous recording is unsupported. Do not assume voicebank legato, RR, keyswitch or dynamic layers survive native SFZ import.

topic: Delay feed output feedback and ducking
session: A retained vocal phrase ending before a later entry. A wet-only mixer delay return and a real dry-vocal AUDIO detector route. Create feed-close, return-close, feedback-change and output-duck candidates from the same phrase. First prove that feed-close leaves existing repeats, while return-close cuts their audible output. Compare compressor recovery revealing the tail with a manual phrase ride. Test seek, stop/restart and re-enable around a nonempty delay line; retain behavior evidence.
check: No duplicate dry signal on return. The selected word alone excites the effect; tail appears in the intended gap. Output ducking is not described as clearing memory. Any unverified flush/reset behavior is left as a gap rather than assumed. Mixer delay ms/percent differs from synth-rack time and mix law. No native bus feedback cycle or hidden feedback-filter control is assumed. render_range bus isolation preserves the rest of the detector graph.

session: A voice or instrument alternating quiet and strong registers, with audible low-level noise. Dry reference and fixed full-mix backing. Check neutral crossover recombination before processing and compare static EQ against band attenuation for an intermittent bloom. In mixer multiband, compare range 0, negative attenuation-only and positive bounded boost/cut on the same band. Keep static makeup fixed while changing dynamic action. Hear attack, following quiet event and noise floor with minimum versus linear phase costs identified.
check: Range zero is correctly identified as neutral. Quiet boost is named below-threshold boost, not upward expansion. No band solo/mute is left active and every candidate is compared recombined. Detector band and stereo Mid/Side are never conflated. Mixer per-band controls are not promised for the shared-control three-band synth compressor. Minimum-phase neutral sum can differ in phase; a non-null is not proof of magnitude error.

session: A raw or minimally processed drum loop with quiet hits, strong attack and cymbal sustain. Dry route plus one return initially, with optional additional distinct paths. Set a return for a named punch/body/grit role using fixed upstream drive and varied return blend. Hear barely audible, fair and excessive amounts at compensated overall level. Remove each added return from the completed mix and state what is lost. Use different blends in sparse and dense sections with explicit reset.
check: The winner adds the intended role without merely winning by loudness. Dry/source audio is summed only through intended paths. Attack, cymbal bleed and quiet hits survive the full-mix blend. One return is enough unless another path has a distinct demonstrated contribution. Latency and wet/dry gain law need verification; parallel is not inherently transient-preserving.

session: Supplied clean melody, pitched grit and unpitched scream textures on a common lyric/section. A dense band arrangement and retained unprocessed vocals. Identify pitched versus noisy regions before tuning, assigning separate clean and texture buses. Compare one essential dynamic stage with a justified second peak/body stage. Add only selected support syllables, then compare clean-to-aggressive transition at matched listening level. Remove support layers and test whether body, width or emphasis is actually lost.
check: Lyrics and melodic target stay clear through transition. Noise/consonants are not forced into scale notes. No unacceptable breath/room lift, harshness or low-mid buildup from added density. No physical scream coaching or mandatory number of takes. Blob segmentation repair and continuous pitch curves are external dependencies.

session: Supplied speech containing quiet and loud phrases, room continuity and edit boundaries. Music bed with a sustained part and a transition under speech. An actual delivery brief or explicitly unresolved destination fields. Compare pre-insert exceptional-word correction with post-processing phrase balance. Compare manual music ride against a verified dialogue-AUDIO-key compressor or relevant dynamic band. Check word ends, pauses and later music recovery without erasing natural room continuity. GUI export/reopen the full file; agent uses contiguous <=600 s windows for review if needed, documenting coverage and version inclusion.
check: No swallowed syllable or syllable-by-syllable music pump. Peak, RMS window, whole-program loudness and gain reduction are described separately. Actual start/end/tail and every required version verified; chunks are not claimed as assembled delivery. Panel excludes render_offline; complete-file export/assembly requires GUI or another verified capability. No autonomous microphone recording, learned restoration, chapter metadata or destination metering is invented.

topic: Modulation base, depth and phase isolation
session: Use one held rich tone with a supported cutoff route. Make a base-value control, a shallow unipolar-depth variation, a bipolar variation and a phase-only variation while holding rate fixed.
check: State which versions change extrema and which move only accent time. Verify actual catalog units and limits; compare note-off and two repeated renders.

topic: Envelope retrigger versus reset from current level
session: Use a long opening gesture and compare detached notes, overlaps, repeats during the rise and release before the peak. Change one supported retrigger or reset setting at a time.
check: Listen to first-hit level and later-hit contour, then seek into the phrase and reopen. A mode name is not acceptance; identify which state the actual engine preserves.

topic: Acid tie, rest, slide and accent independence
session: Build one short pitch motif against fixed drums. Compare versions that independently change a rest to a tie, introduce one overlapping slide, or accent one step through verified amp/filter routes.
check: The pitch order stays fixed while articulation changes are identifiable. Check the note after a rest, the loop return and a mid-phrase start; do not claim a dedicated circuit from ordinary velocity.

session: Use a stereo source with different left/right content. Compare documented center and side balance, then separately change a synth voice allocation. Keep a wet send active for a second routing check.
check: Explain which channel was attenuated and which note voice changed. Verify pre/post-send pan ownership and compare actual mono fold with a documented gain convention.

topic: Mid-side sum and irreversible center cancellation
session: With a supported matrix or verified external analysis, use identical, hard-panned and opposite-polarity channel probes. Record the encode/decode gain convention before comparing the resulting sums.
check: A matching encode/decode reconstructs the source. Removing Side does not restore canceled Mid; meter curves alone do not decide musical mono compatibility.

session: Keep one pulse or low-body anchor fixed and bound the changing timbre source. Render a few short candidates, retain one accepted interval and preserve patch state plus source media.
check: Name the chosen phrase role, exact range and artifact owner. Reopen it and check no duplicate dry path or baked processing; delete only unreferenced scratch under the artifact policy.

topic: Sampler note-off and choke state matrix
session: Map one tonal source and two related chops. Probe short tap, held note, self-retrigger, alternating pads and overlapping voices using the actual supported playback modes and group/off_by routes.
check: Separate note-off tail from transport silence and self-polyphony from cross-pad choke. Check pause/stop/seek and reopening; do not invent an unsupported start-offset opcode.

topic: Root, drum trigger and stable-tail tuning
session: Inspect a pitched-decay drum and a stable tonal sample. Identify a stable tail where possible, set unity-pitch mapping separately from the drum trigger and play two notes around the chosen root.
check: Verify actual output pitch rather than metadata or octave-label convention. A moving attack or chord sample may not have one reliable fundamental; retain that uncertainty.

topic: Procedural clap bursts versus snare body
session: On fixed backbeat events compare a shaped noise hit, several close noise bursts and noise over a pitched body. Keep peak/output level controlled and add room only after choosing the dry articulation.
check: Identify whether source bursts, body or tail makes the family legible. Test a roll and velocity change in context; unsupported FM or comb names are not synthesized results.

topic: Kick pitch contour versus body decay
session: Use a supported oscillator with independent short pitch contour and amplitude decay. Compare changing only pitch depth, only contour duration and only body decay over the same bass line.
check: Hear a stable body and intended onset without assuming every click has a tunable note. Inspect final headroom, the next kick arrival and several rendered notes.

session: Inventory a small authorized pack: full/top, dry/wet, pumped/unpumped, alternate key/tempo and MIDI/preset/source companions where present. Audition the same phrase with two variants while holding other parts fixed.
check: Keep one role-appropriate variant with its source/terms and companion links. Identify printed processing and rhythmic content; do not download every variant or infer clearance from a pack label.

topic: Mixed-fidelity foreground and wet texture hierarchy
session: Keep a clean foreground phrase and compare a continuous colored bed, sparse texture events and coloring of a wet return only. Hold source notes and monitor level fixed.
check: The foreground and silence remain intelligible. Describe which texture supplies place, contrast or motion; codec artifacts, bit reduction and rate reduction are distinct choices.

session: Create an original four-bar reconstruction, a separate authorized comparison reference, and any source material deliberately retained in the arrangement. Render the candidate with every comparison-only path excluded, including direct routes, sends and returns. Test each role by ablation, restore the intended candidate, and compare it with the separate reference at two aligned landmarks.
check: The comparison full mix contributes nothing to candidate playback/export. Intended retained stems still contribute. Bus labels, separate lanes and a mute button are not sufficient evidence of exclusion; inspect actual paths and hear the candidate separately at compensated listening gain.

topic: Playing parts versus stored project history
session: Inspect an authorized project passage containing a muted reference, source MIDI, an alternate take and a printed or frozen tail. Build an inventory of only paths that can contribute in that passage, preserving separate source and arrangement coordinates.
check: Verify each proposed role by omission and restoration. A cache or long stored note list must not inflate the count; record missing-resource and note-chase uncertainty.

session: Make a four-pad kit and a phrase whose first draft deliberately uses a different key map. Inspect receiving keys, repair only the map or notes, then compare short taps, held notes and repeated hits.
check: Every intended hit triggers its documented source; unused keys remain silent. Changing compression or gain must not be accepted as fixing an unmapped note.

session: Compare zero-duration imported events with explicit short notes on the same one-shot and envelope-following sample modes. Preserve the source range and note-off settings.
check: Report actual trigger and tail behavior for the supported instrument. Do not infer equivalence from the original host name, imported label or visible MIDI event.

topic: Bass call and response from one sample region bank
session: Take one authorized expressive bass source and retain three distinct regions. Keep a stable mono low part while assigning short upper calls, gaps and answers across two bars. Change one region or duration at a time.
check: Audition each source region, then the full phrase with drums. Reject a region that masks the next answer, duplicates a sub attack or clicks at the splice.

session: Choose two sustained loops with different stated keys and tempos plus two unwarped one-shots. Verify tonal centre, source-time mapping and duration independently, then fit them to a short progression.
check: File labels are candidates; listen to the result against bass and at the loop seam. Do not apply sustained-loop warp decisions indiscriminately to transient one-shots.

topic: Sustained shell versus pulsed chord layer
session: Keep one bass progression and lead fixed. Compare a sustained upper shell, a pulsed middle voicing and a sparse top-note layer, first separately and then in chosen combinations.
check: Remove duplicated roots and unnecessary inner notes one at a time. Keep only layers that contribute a distinguishable role at the same overall listening gain.

session: Place a fixed arpeggio over four changing roots. Compare retaining its pedal tones, changing one conflicting pitch and changing only its register or duration.
check: Name the actual intervals at each root and hear the complete phrase. A scale match or faster arpeggio does not establish compatible harmony or useful brightness.

topic: Muted ghost key versus written pump
session: Compare actual kick-key compression, a separate ghost source and supported explicit amplitude automation over a syncopated phrase with a silent kick bar. Keep source sound and level fixed.
check: Record the exact detector tap and mute semantics. The intended mechanism must follow its own events, recover for pickups and remain non-summing if it is only a key.

topic: Local reverb rise with a deliberate reset
session: Give a lead a reverb rise over the final two beats of each short phrase. Restore the intended wet state before the next phrase while allowing any independently owned return tail to decay.
check: Hear the preceding pickup through the next attack, then seek into and reopen the phrase. Verify the wet path and reset state instead of copying an external host's same-time point encoding.

topic: Portable print tails and source isolation
session: Retain an editable source and a short accepted print with a tail. Compare the print while muting its source, then reopen the project with its retained media in the supported durable location.
check: The print is neither doubled nor processed twice; the tail survives the clip boundary. Document whether the capture was an isolated part, bus or full mix.

session: Fit an original short loop to an eight-bar section, duplicate it through a longer section, and compare the first and final downbeats. Retain a deliberately short or long alternative, then reopen the accepted project and replace the source in a copy.
check: Verify the final boundary and source window, not just the first attack or filename tempo. Explain accumulated offset and preserve intentional pickups and tails; the accepted timing must survive reopening and recovery selection.

session: Route an original instrument through two groups. Compare a muted source, disabled lane, bypassed effect, zero-gain parent and disconnected output while preserving the written phrase. Inspect sends separately.
check: Identify the actual cause before changing the patch or adding gain. Restore each temporary state; verify the complete source-to-main path and retained sidechain behavior rather than relying on an enabled strip.

topic: Stored phrase versus selected source window
session: Author a sixteen-bar source with two endings. Place only an internal phrase, keep an unplaced alternative and compare a cropped occurrence with a full occurrence at the same timeline start.
check: Describe source coordinates, selected window and actual arrangement contribution separately. Unplaced notes, tails and backups must not become extra playing roles; verify the selected phrase by omission and restoration.

session: Create a voice-like phrase with optional instrument-stage space, a track effect and a shared return. Make controlled versions that bypass one available stage at a time, retaining a printed version as a separate source.
check: Explain where the tail originates and which stage remains editable. Current insert bypass cannot remove printed space; unavailable or opaque stages stay uncertain. Compare the same word ending and gap at controlled level.

session: Make an original short arrangement with a release tail, a muted sketch and a distant unused control region. Define the intended ending and cover the final audible material in bounded auditions.
check: Choose render and listening bounds from the intended arc and contributing sources plus tails. Do not truncate a release or extend the song solely to a distant inactive or control region; document actual delivered coverage.

session: Extend an original phrase into a second section while retaining local filter, wet-feed and gain gestures. Compare copying only notes/audio with deliberately continuing or resetting each supported automation owner.
check: Hear the seam from the preceding pickup through the next attack, seek into both sections and reopen. Verify target units, source windows, reset anchors and tail ownership; no unexplained stale automation may decide the new section.

session: Use a longer original source with a pickup, a two-beat crop and a later internal-window reprise. Preserve source coordinates while moving clips.
check: Verify the first and last included attacks, pickup and replayed source position. Check held-note chase and release instead of assuming a crop truncates all sound.

topic: Note duration belongs to its pitch
session: Hold one lower note for eight beats and a higher note for two, then exchange their durations without changing onset or pitch set. Compare the complete phrase at fixed gain.
check: Hear the different foundation and top continuity. Verify exact per-note pitch and length records; separate pitch and duration ranges cannot distinguish these arrangements.

topic: Layered sample receivers and saved alternatives
session: Use a supported sampled-instrument mapping with two receiving regions for one trigger and a retained disabled alternative. Inspect source files, region bounds, receiving keys and each pitched source's actual root before isolating each region.
check: Each intended region contributes only under its documented trigger conditions. A region needs no separate MIDI phrase to receive a shared key; restore temporary states. Request a print/export for unsupported source-host fan-out instead of assuming equivalence.

session: Compare a source with enabled zero-wet processing, a bypassed slot, and enabled nonzero-wet processing over the same phrase. Then test a supported automation override separately.
check: Resolve the actual target, wet path and passage activation. Match listening level for each omission before attributing space, dynamics or motion to an effect name; preserve unknown external state explicitly.

topic: Dense retriggers as a bounded stress case
session: Use a tiny original retrigger excerpt with duplicate same-key events and explicit event/voice bounds. Compare source-event playback with an accepted short consolidation at controlled level.
check: Check peaks, attack continuity and tails. Use runtime metrics only when the actual tool exposes them; otherwise leave cost unmeasured. Event polyphony is not unique harmony or quality; stop escalation when it adds no useful role.

session: Retain one authorized short vocal or melodic source. Write a fixed end-of-phrase retrigger grid, then compare one repeated source window with neighboring windows progressing through the original gesture. Keep event count, gain and effects unchanged.
check: Hear the previous word or note, the stutter and next downbeat. Explain whether repeated identity or progressing wording/contour serves the phrase; increasing density must not substitute for that choice. Verify seams and retained source bounds.

topic: Staggered chord attacks with a shared release
session: Author a chord on a simple sustained sound with staggered note starts. Compare equal note lengths against individually shortened gates that share a release, then place both under the same bass change.
check: Describe attack spread, overlap and phrase release separately. Hear whether the prior chord clouds the new bass or the shared cutoff feels abrupt; hold sound and gain fixed and verify actual onset-duration pairs.

session: Use an original recorded or synthesized phrase and a retained processed version. Let an intact phrase end before a later chopped answer. Move each supported control gesture with its intended region and compare an intentional gap with continuous overlap.
check: Hear the entire handoff and next repeat. Retain source/effect ownership, avoid unintended print-plus-source doubling and double processing, and verify the gap, first attack, wet resets and tail in the reopened project.

topic: Uniform gate scaling versus phrase-specific releases
session: Author an upper phrase over a supporting figure. Keep the support, upper pitches, attacks and velocities fixed. Compare uniformly shortened gates with individually held chord anchors and short passing notes; preserve a full and a cropped ending.
check: Verify actual note-duration pairs and which events fall inside the selected window. Hear continuity, articulation and the next entrance with the actual envelope; a sustain label or longer written gate does not establish a longer audible note.

topic: Full piano interlude to melody-only return
session: Write an original piano interlude with bass, inner harmony and melody. Reuse its identity over an ensemble that now supplies the low and chord roles. Compare the full piano part, melody alone and melody with one selected inner answer.
check: Hear the interlude and ensemble return at matched listening gain. Identify which role each piano layer contributes; retain recognizable phrasing while avoiding redundant low attacks or harmonic masking.

topic: Exchange pulsed and sustained roles across sections
session: Keep one original harmonic map, bass anchor and melodic landmark. In one section pulse the upper role over a sustained middle part; in the next exchange those activities. Compare with making every layer busy.
check: Identify which role owns rhythmic motion in each section. Check actual envelopes and note releases, harmonic continuity, foreground focus and the handoff; additional events alone do not establish a stronger section.

session: Author a short arp with one register apex and an ending that releases energy. Separately compare even versus shaped velocity, a denser quiet ending, and brief bursts versus continuous notes under fixed lead and chords.
check: Calibrate the patch response to velocity. Hear the apex, retreat and next entrance at fixed track gain. Choose breathing space and articulation that preserve the foreground and fit each actual bass change.

topic: Vocal dialogue from imitation to collective statement
session: Use authorized original vocal fragments for a call, an imitating reply, an independent answer and a final supported statement. Compare retaining an outgoing vowel across the reply with clearing it for a consonant-led answer; finish with an exposed or accompanied coda.
check: Verify source mapping, pitch/formant character, word or gesture intelligibility, overlap, transient density and final release by listening. A delayed duplicate remains one recorded performance; use independently supplied voices when that is the intended role.

session: Keep an original lead continuous while comparing a shared accompaniment cut, a brief support gap with drum punctuation, and staggered layer withdrawal. Keep the harmony and monitoring level fixed, assigning which dry part or wet tail carries the transition.
check: Hear the preceding phrase through the next arrival. Identify the bridge role, actual release and any surviving return; the gap must express a chosen phrase gesture instead of an accidental held chord or leftover effect.

session: Keep an original phrase unchanged and add a delayed answer in another register. Compare a complete shifted copy with a reply that omits a crowded event and has its own ending, using distinct supported sounds at controlled gain.
check: Verify pitch, onset, duration and velocity per event, then hear the repeated phrase and following entrance. Preserve the original identity while choosing the response density, harmonic fit and final release deliberately.
